svg.aria-label: Fig. M5 How uops pack into retire groups, and what the window probes see
svg.text: Fig. M5 How uops pack into retire groups, and what the window probes see
The packing rule is inferred from knees in the window probes. The arithmetic below shows where the rule fits and where it does not.
A uop stream in program order
shaded uops issue; nop and b take a retire slot but no issue slot (confirmed)
Packed by the rule: a memory op starts a group, a branch ends one, at most 7 slots, at most 4 issuing
closed by the str that follows
Group 1 holds 4 issuing uops (ldr add sub b.eq); a fifth
issuing uop would have forced a new group (rule, inferred).
Group entry (proposed): 7 uop slots with done bits, a count of
map changing uops to pop from the history file, an exception
slot, and a branch flag; retire pops up to 8 groups a cycle.
Handley reads the same knees as one failable slot per row
(a row retires only when its single memory op or branch is
done). The two readings differ on whether 2 memory ops
can share a row. Test: a stream of pairs ldr ldr nop nop nop
nop nop gives 330 x 7 under one row per memory op and
330 x 3.5 if each ldr opens its own row.
Load and non speculative store queue entries are released before retire (inferred), so the LSQ
is not what holds a group open; the group waits for the done bits of its issuing uops.
fits: the probe loop itself uses about 33 slots
does not fit 4 per group; fits 3 per group, or 4 with a 1000 entry issuing uop limit elsewhere
rename retire queue, 16 retired per cycle
fits; this is the second queue
fits a branch checkpoint table of 144 (proposed)
knee moves with the delay used (125 under DRAM, 188 under store address), the signature of allocation at issue
380 total less what the probe keeps live

The issuing filler discrepancy is the most useful open item here: either groups hold 3 issuing uops, not 4, or a separate 1000 entry structure (scheduler plus dispatch total is 134 + 72 + 48, far short) limits issuing uops.
